source.primary_manuscript: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments, 4th c. CE ~330-360). NB: Codex Vaticanus (B/03) does NOT contain Revelation in its original 4th-c. hand.
source.secondary_manuscript: Codex Alexandrinus (A/02; British Library Royal 1 D. V-VIII, 5th c. CE) — for Revelation, often preferred to Sinaiticus on internal grounds. Codex Ephraemi Rescriptus (C/04; 5th c., palimpsest).
source.early_papyri_cross_collation: P47 (Chester Beatty III; 3rd c. CE ~250) preserves Rev 9:10-17:2 — does NOT preserve Rev 4. P115 (P.Oxy 4499; 3rd-4th c.) preserves portions of Rev 2-15 but is lacunose for ch. 4. For Rev 4 specifically, the earliest substantial witnesses are the 4th-c. Sinaiticus + 5th-c. Alexandrinus + Ephraemi.
source.reference_critical_apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017). Hoskier 1929 for Revelation-specific variants.
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly Koine Greek transliteration (SBL convention): polytonic-stripped lowercase Latin with diacritics for breathings (h- for rough; nothing for smooth) and Greek-specific letters (ē for eta, ō for omega, ph for phi, ch for chi, ps for psi, th for theta, rh for rho with rough breathing); ai/ei/oi/au/eu/ou diphthongs preserved; accent marks generally omitted in scholarly translit
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Sinaiticus + Alexandrinus + Ephraemi original codicology + the NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus + Hoskier 1929
source.fetchedFrom: SBLGNT public-domain edition (Holmes 2010) + NA28 reference + Hoskier 1929.
source.citation: Aland, Aland, Karavidopoulos, Martini, Metzger, eds., *Novum Testamentum Graece*, 28th ed. (Nestle-Aland, Stuttgart 2012). UBS5 = Aland et al., *The Greek New Testament*, 5th ed. (United Bible Societies 2014). Holmes, M. W., ed., *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (SBL 2010; public-domain). Jongkind, D., ed., *The Greek New Testament*, Tyndale House (Crossway 2017). Hoskier, H. C., *Concerning the Text of the Apocalypse*, 2 vols. (Quaritch 1929). Codex Sinaiticus: British Library Add. 43725 + (4th c.). Codex Alexandrinus: British Library Royal 1 D. V-VIII (5th c.). Aune WBC 1997-1998 (vol 1 covers ch. 4); Beale NIGTC 1999; Charles ICC 1920; Koester AB 2014; Mounce NICNT 1997 rev.; Bauckham *The Climax of Prophecy* (T&T Clark 1993); Halperin *The Faces of the Chariot* (Mohr Siebeck 1988) on Merkavah / Shi'ur Qomah background; Rowland *The Open Heaven* (SPCK 1982); Hurtado *One God, One Lord* (Fortress 1988); Levine-Brettler JANT 2017.
source.paleography_note: The Koine Greek text is preserved in polytonic form as transmitted via SBLGNT. Rev 4-5 is the most-densely throne-vision chapter of the NT, with continuous cross-corpus to Ezek 1, Dan 7, Isa 6, and the developing Merkavah/Hekhalot/Shi'ur Qomah throne-mysticism tradition (cf. 1 Enoch 14; 2 Enoch 20-22; 4 Ezra; 3 Enoch). The early Greek manuscripts use scriptio continua. Nomina sacra appear abbreviated.

verses.text: Μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ θύρα ἠνεῳγμένη ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ ἡ φωνὴ ἡ πρώτη ἣν ἤκουσα ὡς σάλπιγγος λαλούσης μετ’ ἐμοῦ λέγων· Ἀνάβα ὧδε, καὶ δείξω σοι ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι μετὰ ταῦτα.
verses.translit: Meta tauta eidon, kai idou thyra ēneōgmenē en tō ouranō, kai hē phōnē hē prōtē hēn ēkousa hōs salpingos lalousēs met’ emou legōn· Anaba hōde, kai deixō soi ha dei genesthai meta tauta.
verses.notes: **MAJOR THRONE-VISION OPENING — DOOR OPENED IN HEAVEN**. *thyra ēneōgmenē en tō ouranō* (a door opened in heaven) — cross-corpus 1 Enoch 14:15 (the opened-heavens throne-vision); 3 Macc 6:18; Test. Levi 5:1; cf. Acts 7:56 (Stephen). *Anaba hōde* (Come up here) + ecstatic-ascent — cross-corpus Ezek 1:1; 2 Cor 12:2-4 (Paul's ascent); 1 Enoch 14:8 (Enoch caught up). *deixō soi ha dei genesthai* — echoes Dan 2:28 LXX + Rev 1:1. **HIGH LENS-RISK FLAG**: the *thyra ēneōgmenē en tō ouranō* + ascent-call is one of the densest engagement-sites in the Raëlian canon (and other heterodox traditions) — read as portal / craft-entry. Acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework MUST be applied. **EDITOR DO NOT PRE-RESOLVE** toward (a) conventional apocalyptic throne-vision reading or (b) Raëlian portal-craft reading.

verses.text: εὐθέως ἐγενόμην ἐν πνεύματι· καὶ ἰδοὺ θρόνος ἔκειτο ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν θρόνον καθήμενος,
verses.translit: eutheōs egenomēn en pneumati· kai idou thronos ekeito en tō ouranō, kai epi ton thronon kathēmenos,
verses.notes: **ECSTATIC-STATE FORMULA + THRONE-IMAGE**. *egenomēn en pneumati* — same trance-formula as 1:10. *thronos ekeito en tō ouranō, kai epi ton thronon kathēmenos* (a throne stood in heaven, and one seated on the throne) — cross-corpus **Ezek 1:26-28** + **Dan 7:9-10** + **Isa 6:1**. The seated-on-the-throne periphrasis avoids direct divine description — Merkavah-style reverential circumlocution. Cross-corpus 1 Enoch 14:18-20 (Enoch's throne-vision).

verses.text: καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ὅμοιος ὁράσει λίθῳ ἰάσπιδι καὶ σαρδίῳ, καὶ ἶρις κυκλόθεν τοῦ θρόνου ὅμοιος ὁράσει σμαραγδίνῳ.
verses.translit: kai ho kathēmenos homoios horasei lithō iaspidi kai sardiō, kai iris kyklothen tou thronou homoios horasei smaragdinō.
verses.notes: **GEMSTONE THEOPHANY**. *iaspidi kai sardiō* (jasper and carnelian — the *odem* and *yashpheh* of the Hebrew Bible). Cross-corpus **Ezek 28:13** LXX (the gemstone-catalog of the King of Tyre / cosmic-priestly figure); Exod 28:17-21 (the high-priestly breastplate with its twelve stones — odem first, yashpheh last); cf. Rev 21:18-21 (the New Jerusalem walls). *iris kyklothen tou thronou … smaragdinō* (rainbow around the throne like emerald) — cross-corpus Ezek 1:28 (the throne-radiance like a rainbow); Gen 9:13-17 (the Noahic rainbow-covenant); cf. Sir 50:7. The chromatic-theophany evokes the visible electromagnetic spectrum encoded in mineralogical-imagery. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: preserve.

verses.text: καὶ κυκλόθεν τοῦ θρόνου θρόνους εἴκοσι τέσσαρες, καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς θρόνους εἴκοσι τέσσαρας πρεσβυτέρους καθημένους περιβεβλημένους ἐν ἱματίοις λευκοῖς, καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν στεφάνους χρυσοῦς.
verses.translit: kai kyklothen tou thronou thronous eikosi tessares, kai epi tous thronous eikosi tessaras presbyterous kathēmenous peribeblēmenous en himatiois leukois, kai epi tas kephalas autōn stephanous chrysous.
verses.notes: **THE TWENTY-FOUR ELDERS**. *eikosi tessaras presbyterous* (24 elders) — interpretive options: (a) 12 patriarchs + 12 apostles (Bauckham 1993); (b) 24 priestly courses (1 Chr 24:7-19); (c) 24 zodiacal/temporal-watchers (Babylonian astronomical-theology — the *ulinnu* judges); (d) celestial-council members (cf. Ps 89:7-8; 1 Kgs 22:19; Job 1:6). White garments + golden crowns. Major Revelation throne-council motif (cf. 4:10; 5:8; 11:16; 19:4).

verses.text: καὶ ἐκ τοῦ θρόνου ἐκπορεύονται ἀστραπαὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ βρονταί· καὶ ἑπτὰ λαμπάδες πυρὸς καιόμεναι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου, ἅ εἰσιν τὰ ἑπτὰ πνεύματα τοῦ θεοῦ,
verses.translit: kai ek tou thronou ekporeuontai astrapai kai phōnai kai brontai· kai hepta lampades pyros kaiomenai enōpion tou thronou, ha eisin ta hepta pneumata tou theou,
verses.notes: **SINAI-THEOPHANY MARKERS + SEVEN-SPIRITS**. *astrapai kai phōnai kai brontai* (lightnings + voices + thunders) — cross-corpus **Exod 19:16** LXX (the Sinai-theophany triad); cf. Rev 8:5; 11:19; 16:18 (the recurring Sinai-formula in Revelation marking apocalyptic-judgment hinges). *hepta lampades pyros … ta hepta pneumata tou theou* (seven torches of fire … the seven spirits of God) — cross-corpus Zech 4:2 (the seven-branched menorah with seven lamps); 1:4.

verses.text: καὶ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου ὡς θάλασσα ὑαλίνη ὁμοία κρυστάλλῳ. Καὶ ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ κύκλῳ τοῦ θρόνου τέσσαρα ζῷα γέμοντα ὀφθαλμῶν ἔμπροσθεν καὶ ὄπισθεν·
verses.translit: kai enōpion tou thronou hōs thalassa hyalinē homoia krystallō. Kai en mesō tou thronou kai kyklō tou thronou tessara zōa gemonta ophthalmōn emprosthen kai opisthen·
verses.notes: **GLASS SEA + FOUR LIVING CREATURES**. *thalassa hyalinē homoia krystallō* (sea of glass like crystal) — cross-corpus **Ezek 1:22** LXX (the firmament over the chayyot heads, *hōsei horasis krystallou*); cf. Exod 24:10 (the sapphire-pavement under God's feet); 2 Enoch 3 (Enoch's crystal-floor heaven). *tessara zōa* (four living creatures) — THE CHAYYOT of Ezekiel. *gemonta ophthalmōn emprosthen kai opisthen* (full of eyes before and behind) — cross-corpus **Ezek 1:18** LXX (chayyot wheels full of eyes); cf. Ezek 10:12. **MAJOR LENS-RISK FLAG**: the four-living-creatures vision is the densest single-pericope engagement-site for ancient-astronaut readings (Däniken, Sitchin) AND for the Shi'ur Qomah throne-mysticism tradition (where the chayyot have 64 faces each). Raëlian canon engages this passage. Preserve at surface; document cross-corpus.

verses.text: καὶ τὸ ζῷον τὸ πρῶτον ὅμοιον λέοντι, καὶ τὸ δεύτερον ζῷον ὅμοιον μόσχῳ, καὶ τὸ τρίτον ζῷον ἔχων τὸ πρόσωπον ὡς ἀνθρώπου, καὶ τὸ τέταρτον ζῷον ὅμοιον ἀετῷ πετομένῳ.
verses.translit: kai to zōon to prōton homoion leonti, kai to deuteron zōon homoion moschō, kai to triton zōon echōn to prosōpon hōs anthrōpou, kai to tetarton zōon homoion aetō petomenō.
verses.notes: **FOUR FACES — LION / OX / HUMAN / EAGLE**. Cross-corpus **Ezek 1:10** LXX (the chayyot four-faced description: ox, lion, eagle, human — order varies). Each Revelation-creature has ONE face (vs. Ezek's four-each); Revelation distributes Ezek's quadruple-face across four separate creatures. **PATRISTIC INTERPRETATION**: Irenaeus *Adv. Haer.* 3.11.8 assigns these to the four Gospels: Matthew = human (Davidic genealogy), Mark = lion (wilderness-voice), Luke = ox (priestly), John = eagle (heavenly). This is the source of the Western iconographic-tradition. **SHI'UR QOMAH BACKGROUND**: the developing Merkavah-mysticism tradition (cf. 3 Enoch 17-26; Sefer Hekhalot) amplifies the chayyot to monumental cosmic scale; Rev 4 is one of the formative texts of this tradition (Halperin 1988). **LENS-RISK FLAG**: preserve.

verses.text: καὶ τὰ τέσσαρα ζῷα, ἓν καθ’ ἓν αὐτῶν ἔχων ἀνὰ πτέρυγας ἕξ, κυκλόθεν καὶ ἔσωθεν γέμουσιν ὀφθαλμῶν· καὶ ἀνάπαυσιν οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς λέγοντες· Ἅγιος ἅγιος ἅγιος κύριος ὁ θεός ὁ παντοκράτωρ, ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος.
verses.translit: kai ta tessara zōa, hen kath’ hen autōn echōn ana pterygas hex, kyklothen kai esōthen gemousin ophthalmōn· kai anapausin ouk echousin hēmeras kai nyktos legontes· Hagios hagios hagios kyrios ho theos ho pantokratōr, ho ēn kai ho ōn kai ho erchomenos.
verses.notes: **THE TRISAGION — *HAGIOS HAGIOS HAGIOS***. Each creature has six wings (cross-corpus **Isa 6:2** LXX — the seraphim's six wings, NOT Ezek's chayyot four wings; Revelation conflates Ezekiel + Isaiah). *Hagios hagios hagios kyrios ho theos ho pantokratōr* — direct cross-corpus **Isa 6:3** LXX (*Hagios hagios hagios kyrios sabaōth*) — the seraphic trisagion. Revelation substitutes *pantokratōr* for *sabaōth*. The triple-holy + temporal-formula (*ho ēn kai ho ōn kai ho erchomenos* — past/present/future, slight variant of 1:4 order) becomes the foundational text for Eastern + Western Christian liturgical Sanctus (the Eucharistic prayer's trisagion). **MAJOR THEOLOGICAL-LITURGICAL SITE**. Aune WBC 1.302-305.

verses.text: Καὶ ὅταν δώσουσιν τὰ ζῷα δόξαν καὶ τιμὴν καὶ εὐχαριστίαν τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ, τῷ ζῶντι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων,
verses.translit: Kai hotan dōsousin ta zōa doxan kai timēn kai eucharistian tō kathēmenō epi tō thronō, tō zōnti eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn,
verses.notes: Doxology-triad: glory + honor + thanks. *tō zōnti eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn* — cross-corpus Dan 4:34 LXX; 6:26; 12:7.

verses.text: πεσοῦνται οἱ εἴκοσι τέσσαρες πρεσβύτεροι ἐνώπιον τοῦ καθημένου ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου, καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν τῷ ζῶντι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, καὶ βαλοῦσιν τοὺς στεφάνους αὐτῶν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου λέγοντες·
verses.translit: pesountai hoi eikosi tessares presbyteroi enōpion tou kathēmenou epi tou thronou, kai proskynēsousin tō zōnti eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn, kai balousin tous stephanous autōn enōpion tou thronou legontes·
verses.notes: **TWENTY-FOUR ELDERS CASTING CROWNS**. *balousin tous stephanous autōn enōpion tou thronou* (will cast their crowns before the throne) — vassalage / submission-of-royalty ritual. Cross-corpus Tacitus *Ann.* 15.29 (Tiridates of Armenia laying his diadem before Nero's image in 66 CE — possible historical-imperial-cult background).

verses.text: Ἄξιος εἶ, ὁ κύριος καὶ ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν, λαβεῖν τὴν δόξαν καὶ τὴν τιμὴν καὶ τὴν δύναμιν, ὅτι σὺ ἔκτισας τὰ πάντα, καὶ διὰ τὸ θέλημά σου ἦσαν καὶ ἐκτίσθησαν.
verses.translit: Axios ei, ho kyrios kai ho theos hēmōn, labein tēn doxan kai tēn timēn kai tēn dynamin, hoti sy ektisas ta panta, kai dia to thelēma sou ēsan kai ektisthēsan.
verses.notes: **CREATION-HYMN**. *Axios ei* (Worthy art thou) — worship-acclamation formula; cf. Rev 5:9, 12 (the Lamb-acclamations). *ho kyrios kai ho theos hēmōn* (the Lord and the God of us) — note the striking parallel to Domitian's self-styling *dominus et deus noster* (Suetonius *Domitian* 13.2), traditionally read as Revelation's subversive contrast: the true cosmic Lord-and-God vs. the imperial pretender. *ektisas ta panta* (you created all things) — creation-claim. *dia to thelēma sou ēsan kai ektisthēsan* (by your will they existed and were created) — voluntarist creation-theology. Chapter ends, setting up the Lamb-arrival in Rev 5.
